 KOIN Portland Follow Landslides on Oregon Coast close Little Elk Mountain Road for the rainy season
 Rose Hinchliff Mon, October 26, 2026 at 10:56 PM UTC 1 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. PORTLAND, Ore. ( KOIN ) – An encroaching landslide caused by rain poses a threat to public safety, closing Little Elk Mountain Road in Lane County's Coast Range for the winter, Bureau of Land Management officials announced on Monday.
 A landslide threatens to encroach on the road around mile marker 1.4 as heavy rain forecasts dominate the rest of the season. Also referred to as BLM Road 16-8-36, officials said beginning around Nov. 1, they will post warning signs and a closure order as they block off the road.
 BLM officials detailed how eroding soil steepened an already problematic drop-off adjacent to the road and winter weather will compromise the hillside's safety.
 Little Elk Mountain Road landslide (Courtesy Bureau of Land Management)

 Little Elk Mountain Road landslide (Courtesy Bureau of Land Management)
 Because officials believe the slides will continue, the road will remain closed throughout the rainy season, which they estimate will end around May 1.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Landslides regularly impact this road and officials closed the area for this very same reason in both 2021 and April of 2023.
 The Coast Range commonly experiences landslides "due to the underlying geology where shallow soils overlay hard, fractured sandstone," officials explained. They continued, "Wet conditions and damaged vegetation—from wildfire, ice storms, or other disturbance—can create sudden, fast-moving debris flows on these steep slopes."
